Uncover some of the CIA's most secret missions. Each episode tells the real story behind these covert operations. Here's a quick look at what each episode is about:

Learn about the CIA's mission to capture Che Guevara, the famous revolutionary. The CIA sent agent Félix Rodríguez to Bolivia to bring Che back alive because of his strong anti-American views. This episode reveals the true story of the mission using newly released documents.

snippet.title: CIA Declassified: The Beirut Bomb
snippet.description:
Uncover the explosive true story behind the Beirut embassy bombing and the CIA’s covert war with Hezbollah. Espionage, revenge, and intelligence failures rocked America’s response.

This gripping documentary reveals how a series of deadly attacks in 1980s Beirut—including the Marine barracks and US embassy bombings—triggered the CIA’s most secretive and controversial missions. Discover the untold saga of CIA Director William Casey, off-the-books operations, and the targeted attempt to assassinate Sheikh Mohammed Fadlallah, the man believed to lead Hezbollah’s terror network. Explore how a flawed quest for vengeance saw alliances with Mossad and Saudi intelligence, ultimately culminating in a tragic car bomb that missed its target but killed scores of civilians. 

Listen to firsthand accounts from survivors, agents, and experts as they recount the intelligence failures, the rise of Hezbollah, Iran’s covert role, and the devastating impact on US operatives like CIA station chief William Buckley. Learn how these events sparked the creation of the CIA’s Counterterrorism Center and paved the way for modern drone warfare. Perfect for those fascinated by Middle East history, US foreign policy, and the shadowy world of intelligence, this video exposes the real lessons learned from America’s darkest hours in Beirut.

snippet.title: Classified Spy Operations: Inside Cold War Espionage | Extra Long Documentary
snippet.description:
From the aftermath of World War II to the brink of nuclear war in the 1980s, The Spying Game reveals the covert operations that shaped the Cold War. Across three episodes, this full-length documentary uncovers how spies, double agents, and military observers turned divided Germany into the front line of global espionage.
Beginning in the 1950s and 60s, the documentary explores how East and West deployed thousands of intelligence agents to gather crucial information amid escalating fears of mutual assured destruction. Some spies tracked troop movements; others smuggled out nuclear secrets. As tensions rose, Western intelligence turned its focus on East Germany - the Warsaw Pact’s strategic stronghold - using both trained professionals and amateur “travel spies” to monitor Soviet military deployments. By the 1970s, data on tank divisions, call signs, and vehicle types became central to NATO’s understanding of Soviet strength.
The story culminates in the early 1980s, as the Cold War reaches its most dangerous peak. In 1983, NATO’s military exercise Able Archer was misinterpreted by the Soviet Union as a possible prelude to a nuclear first strike. On the edge of disaster, a single double agent helped avert global catastrophe by clarifying NATO’s true intentions.
This is the hidden history of Cold War intelligence - how secrecy, strategy, and subterfuge helped maintain a fragile peace in an age of nuclear fear.

The U.S. has lost more spies and informants since 2010 than at any other time since the Cold War. Leaders of German intelligence agencies also acknowledge that they have once again fallen upon tough times. Money, data and access are proving to be major factors in determining who actually wields power. The 2016 U.S. election made this clear: U.S. intelligence agencies are certain that Russian intelligence helped elect Donald Trump.

And what does that mean for political hot spots and potential conflicts with China, Iran, and Russia? And for allies like Saudi Arabia and Turkey? Will Western intelligence agencies regain the power they once exerted? Wars fought with drone and hacker attacks, increasingly delegated power, and surveillance could push these conflicts to their tipping point.

snippet.title: 4 Hours Of CIA Hunting 20th-Century Infamous Killers And Exposing Dark Secrets
snippet.description:
In this compelling continuation of the series, explore the hidden operations of the CIA as they pursued some of the most infamous figures of the 20th century.

Episode 1 | Killing 'Mad Dog' Gaddafi:
In 2011, the world witnessed the fall of Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi during a brutal civil war. However, what remains largely hidden is the fact that the CIA had been plotting to incite a Libyan uprising for three decades. The rebel leader who eventually toppled Gaddafi had long been a covert ally of the CIA.

Episode 2 | Fortress of War:
Uncovered is the classified tale of two CIA operatives who found themselves in a life-or-death struggle while pursuing Osama bin Laden. Facing overwhelming odds, they managed to quell a Taliban uprising in a remote Afghan fortress. Outnumbered 100-to-1, one of the agents made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty.

Episode 3 | The Real Zero Dark Thirty:
The hunt for Osama bin Laden is a story that has been told many times, but the full truth remains in the shadows. Through the accounts of those who were directly involved from the beginning, this episode unveils the declassified reality behind the 15-year pursuit of the world's most wanted man.

Episode 4: The Hunt For Che Guevara reveals the secret mission launched by the CIA to capture the revolutionary leader Che Guevara. Concerned by Guevara's anti-American stance, the agency dispatched agent Félix Rodríguez to Bolivia with orders to bring him back alive. Newly uncovered documents shed light on the true story of this high-stakes manhunt.

In 1986, a chilling revelation sent shockwaves through the FBI's Soviet counterintelligence section in Washington. Two prized Soviet informants, Valery Martynov and Sergei Motorin, had been compromised. Once exposed, the men were lured back to Moscow, and brutally executed - a bullet in the head for each, the KGB's grim signature for traitors.

The loss of the two agents referred to affectionately within the FBI as ‘M&M’ marked an abrupt end to what had become routine covert meetings and intelligence exchanges.

Parallel to this, the CIA, ensconced across the Potomac in Langley, grappled with its own nightmare. Over the years, dozens of their operatives in the Soviet Union had suddenly gone dark, were executed or imprisoned.

The FBI scrambled to form an elite investigative team to unravel the mystery. Yet, as the years wore on and the puzzle remained unsolved, the unsettling possibility of the traitor being one of their own lingered in the air like a bad smell.

Determined to root out the mole, experienced analysts within the FBI’s Soviet unit delved into archives of debriefings and reports, searching for a pattern, a clue, anything that might reveal a link to the betrayer. They honed in on an innocent agent, meanwhile the culprit, who was outwardly a devout Catholic, a loving husband, father of 6, and a trusted FBI agent, harboured a perilous secret. 

Robert Philip Hanssen’s decades-long path of treachery is considered the worst intelligence disaster in FBI history. This is his story.

snippet.title: US Embassy Bombings: The CIA's First Hunt for Al-Qaeda | CIA Declassified | FD History
snippet.description:
CIA Declassified - Episode 6: Operation Celestial Balance | History Documentary

Watch the next 'CIA Declassified' episode here: https://youtu.be/DFGm-K-8MWk

In this episode:
In August 1998, coordinated bombings struck the United States embassies in Nairobi, Kenya, and Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, killing hundreds of people and drawing renewed attention to the growing threat posed by Al-Qaeda. As investigators worked to identify those responsible, the search led to an unlikely battleground: Somalia.

Still reeling from years of civil war and largely beyond the reach of foreign governments, Somalia presented enormous challenges for intelligence agencies seeking to track Al-Qaeda operatives believed to be operating within its borders. To gather information and pursue suspected militants, the CIA relied on local allies, paid informants, and emerging surveillance technologies in an effort to penetrate one of the world's most unstable regions.

Combining first-hand accounts with newly available information, this documentary examines the covert operations, difficult choices, and uncertain intelligence that shaped the early pursuit of Al-Qaeda in East Africa and the Horn of Africa in the years before 9/11.


These are the inside stories of America's most top secret covert operations. They involve assassins, deep undercover agents and the CIA's ultra-secret special black ops division. Each film is based upon the CIA's own documents and insider accounts from agents who were there. They show how America's spymasters tracked down and eliminated their nation's enemies.

In this episode:

From 2018, Cooper’s interview with Justice and FBI officials who reveal how they caught a former CIA officer spying for the Chinese.
